info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package tel is the telecommunications surface: phone numbers, calls and messages, on whatever carrier the deployment is configured for.

get.summary: Lists the calls this org has placed or received, newest first.
get.description:
Lists the calls this org has placed or received, newest first. Like the
message list beside it, these are our own records rather than the carrier's.

post.description:
Dials. An `agent` names a Hanzo assistant to answer it; the call is
refused up front when no assistant plane is configured, because a call that
connects to silence has already cost the person who answered it.

delete.summary: Ends a call this org placed.
delete.description:
Ends a call this org placed. The holding is read for THIS org before the
carrier is asked, for the reason releaseNumber gives one surface up: an id
belonging to another tenant would otherwise be hung up by whoever guessed it.

get.summary: Lists the messages this org has sent or received, newest first.
get.description:
Lists the messages this org has sent or received, newest first. Records from
our own store, not the carrier's — so it is what this platform did on the
org's behalf, which is the set an audit or a bill has to agree with.

post.summary: Sends a message from one of this org's own numbers.
post.description:
Sends a message from one of this org's own numbers.

`from` must be a number the org HOLDS, checked against the store rather than
taken on trust — a caller that could send from any number could impersonate
one, and the carrier would deliver it. `to` is required, and the body needs
text or media, because a message with neither is delivered as nothing and
billed as something.

get.summary: Lists the phone numbers this org HOLDS — the ones it has bought and not released.
get.description:
Lists the phone numbers this org HOLDS — the ones it has bought and not
released. Distinct from the availability search one path down
(`/numbers/available`), which asks the carrier what could be bought: this
answers only from our own store, so it is what an org owns rather than what
it could own.

post.summary: Provisions with the carrier FIRST and records second.
post.description:
Provisions with the carrier FIRST and records second. The other order
records a holding that may not exist, and a number the platform believes it owns
but cannot use is worse than one it failed to buy.

get.summary: Asks the carrier what is available to buy.
get.description:
Asks the carrier what is available to buy. Nothing is recorded —
a search is not a holding, and treating it as one is how inventory leaks.

delete.summary: Checks the holding is THIS org's before it reaches the carrier.
delete.description:
Checks the holding is THIS org's before it reaches the carrier.
Without that read, an id belonging to another tenant would be released by
whoever guessed it.

get.summary: Counts what this org holds on the telephony plane: its numbers, its calls and its messages.
get.description:
Counts what this org holds on the telephony plane: its numbers, its calls and
its messages. The one read a dashboard makes before it asks for any list, so
it answers three totals and no rows.

agent.description:
Agent names the Hanzo assistant handling the call. Set means the call was
answered by that assistant rather than connected to a person.

from.description:
From is the calling number in E.164. It must be one this org holds: a carrier
refuses an origination from a number nobody proved they own.

id.description: ID is the carrier's handle for the call — what a hangup or a lookup names.

org.description: Org is the tenant the call was placed for or received by.

status.description:
Status is where the call is: "queued", "ringing", "answered", "completed" or
"failed". Only the last two are terminal.

to.description: To is the called number in E.164.

capable.description:
Capable is what the number can carry: any of "voice", "sms", "mms", "fax". A
number missing "sms" cannot send one no matter what this platform does.

country.description:
Country is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code the number is issued under. Numbering is
national, so this is what makes a search answerable at all.

currency.description:
Currency is the ISO 4217 code Monthly is denominated in. Without it the number
beside it means nothing, so the two are always read together.

e164.description:
E164 is the number in E.164: a leading + and digits only, no spaces or dashes.
That is what a carrier accepts and what a search result must be bought by.

id.description:
ID is the carrier's handle for the number, and the id every route here
addresses it by. It is not the number itself — see E164.

monthly.description:
Monthly is the recurring rental in the MINOR unit of Currency (cents for USD),
exactly as the carrier quoted it. It is a price, not a charge: nothing is billed
by this field.

org.description:
Org is the tenant holding the number. A search result carries none — nobody
holds it yet — which is how an available number is told from a held one.

type.description:
Type is what kind of number it is: "local", "national", "tollfree" or "mobile".
It decides both price and what a carrier will let it originate.

from.description: From is the sending number in E.164, and must be one this org holds.

id.description: ID is the carrier's handle for the message.

org.description: Org is the tenant the message was sent for or received by.

status.description:
Status is where the message is: "queued", "sent", "delivered" or "failed".
"sent" means the carrier took it; "delivered" means the handset got it, and
not every carrier or destination reports that.

text.description: Text is the message body. Empty is legal when the message carried only media.

to.description: To is the receiving number in E.164.

e164.description:
E164 is the number to buy, in E.164 (a leading + and digits), exactly as the
search returned it. This is the number itself, not the id from a search result.

agent.description:
Agent hands the answered call to a Hanzo assistant by name instead of
connecting it to a person. Empty places an ordinary call.

from.description: From is the number to call FROM, in E.164. It must be one this org holds.

record.description:
Record is a per-call flag rather than a product. Where a recording lands and
how long it is kept is the org's retention policy, not this call's.

to.description: To is the number to call, in E.164.

webhook.description:
Webhook is a URL the carrier posts this call's events to as it progresses.
Empty means the call's outcome is only visible by reading it back.

data.description:
Data is this org's own calls, newest first — what this platform placed or
received on its behalf, which is our record rather than the carrier's.

from.description:
From is the number to send FROM, in E.164. It must be one this org holds and it
must be sms-capable.

media.description:
Media are URLs to attach. A message with any is an MMS to the carrier — the
distinction is the carrier's to make, not something the caller declares.

text.description: Text is the message body. It may be empty when Media carries the message.

to.description: To is the number to send to, in E.164.

data.description:
Data is this org's own messages, newest first — from our store rather than the
carrier's, so it is the set an audit or a bill has to agree with.

Data is the numbers, and which numbers depends on the route: a search answers
what the carrier has available, a list answers what this org already holds.

calls.description:
Calls is how many calls this org has placed or received, over its whole
history — a running total, not a window.

messages.description: Messages is the same running total for messages.

numbers.description: Numbers is how many numbers this org holds right now.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
